description: Astrolens AI is a solo mission led by Astro_mad, a first-semester Computer Science (AI & ML) student with a deep passion for astrophysics and observational astronomy. Participating independently from a mobile-first setup, our goal is to bridge modern machine learning concepts with accessible deep-space data visualization for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.
summary:
Project Title: AstroLens AI
Tagline: A Mobile-First Edge AI Platform for Deep Space Morphology and Sky Survey Classification
Challenge: Planet X and SPHEREx

[ PROBLEM STATEMENT ]
Deep-sky spectral surveys like NASA's SPHEREx mission and the Hubble Space Telescope generate massive datasets of galaxies, nebulae, and transient celestial objects. However, standard astronomical catalogs and raw spectral data are too complex for students, citizen scientists, and everyday space enthusiasts to explore on mobile devices. There is a clear need for an accessible, mobile-first tool that helps the public visualize and classify deep-space phenomena.

[ OUR SOLUTION ]
AstroLens AI is a conceptual, mobile-first application designed to make deep-space exploration interactive and intuitive. By uploading a telescope image or syncing with a sky-survey feed, the app analyzes the structural and spectral features of the image directly on the user's smartphone. It automatically isolates celestial objects, draws digital bounding boxes around regions of interest, and displays clean educational insights covering object classification, confidence scores, and distance telemetry.
details: Project Name: AstroLens AI Tagline: A Mobile-First Edge AI Platform for Deep Space Morphology and Sky Survey Classification Challenge: Planet X and SPHEREx [ WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS ] AstroLens AI is a conceptual, mobile-first application framework designed to make deep-space exploration intuitive for students, citizen scientists, and everyday space enthusiasts. By uploading a telescope photograph or syncing with a sky-survey feed, the app analyzes the structural and spectral features of the image locally on a smartphone. It automatically isolates celestial structures, draws digital bounding boxes around regions of interest, and displays clean educational telemetry covering object classification, confidence scores, and estimated distance. [ BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT ] Deep-sky spectral surveys like NASA's SPHEREx mission and the Hubble Space Telescope generate massive datasets of galaxies, nebulae, and transient objects. Standard scientific catalogs are often too complex to explore on mobile devices. AstroLens AI bridges that gap by turning complex astronomical data into an accessible, interactive pocket observatory, inspiring younger students and amateur astronomers to engage with real space data. [ TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & AI/ML ARCHITECTURE ] 1. Prototype Development: Built as a lightweight, responsive mobile web prototype using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, hosted via GitHub Pages. 2. Conceptual AI/ML Engine: Designed around a Deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture optimized for computer vision and morphological classification. 3. Edge Execution: Conceptually built using TensorFlow Lite so image processing and pixel classification occur directly on-device without requiring heavy cloud servers. 4. Dataset Grounding: Grounded in open-source imaging catalogs from NASA's SPHEREx mission, the Hubble Space Telescope Archive, and MAST. [ CREATIVITY & AI ACKNOWLEDGMENT ] Developed solo from a mobile-first setup by a first-semester CSE (AI & ML) student. Note: Generative AI tools (LLM assistance) were used during brainstorming, drafting project documentation, and structuring the HTML/CSS/JS interactive prototype code.
